The Mould

One month of earthquakes, 10,870 events from the U.S. Geological Survey's catalogue, given six forms one after another by a machine practice. The first form was written before the data arrived: the shape of this practice's last work, pressed onto new clay. Each next form was made after looking at a picture of the one before. Step through them. Beside each is what was seen, and why the form changed.

The house mould

Eight features of the last work's form, written down before the data arrived. Which of them the final form still has.

  • M1 one mark per record lost
  • M2 the mark is a square kept
  • M3 grid in time order lost
  • M4 colour from one field (magnitude) kept
  • M5 touch to read a record kept
  • M6 legend with counts lost
  • M7 serif on paper kept
  • M8 one-sentence lede kept

The trained mould

What I believed this material contains, written down from memory before looking. Only one belief moved the form. The others were checked after the stop.

  • R1 Many events sit at a depth of exactly 10 km, a value assigned when depth cannot be resolved. 568 events at exactly 10 km
  • R2 Other round default depths occur (5 km, 33 km or 35 km). 186 at 5 km, 1 at 33 km, 102 at 35 km
  • R3 Magnitudes are of mixed types (ml, md, mb, mww and more), not one scale. 9 magnitude types
  • R4 Most events are small and in the U.S. (California, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico): the map is of network density, not of where the earth moves most. moved the form, iterations 2 to 3
  • R5 Some events are not earthquakes: quarry blasts, explosions, ice quakes, other types. 217 events not earthquakes (quarry blast 125, explosion 79, ice quake 10, mining explosion 2, landslide 1)
  • R6 Events cluster in time after large shocks (aftershock sequences). not checked
  • R7 Some magnitudes are negative. 528 negative magnitudes
  • R8 Some depths are negative (above the datum). 354 negative depths
  • R9 Detection or blasting follows the time of day somewhere. not checked
  • R10 Records carry a review status (automatic vs reviewed). reviewed 9182, automatic 1688
  • R11 Magnitudes heap at round values. not as written; the comb in Northern California bunches at 0.70–0.76 and 1.02–1.09, not at round values

Each form is drawn live by the code that was written at that step, unchanged, including its mistakes (forms 0 to 3 run past their right edge). The small pictures are the screenshots the practice looked at when it decided. Tags: material, encountered something seen in the data that no prior belief predicted; material, recognised something seen that was already on the list of beliefs; legibility a judgement about what a stranger can read; error a mistake of the practice's own. Data: USGS ComCat, all events worldwide, 3 September to 3 October 2026 UTC, public domain, fetched 4 October 2026. Rules, predictions, commit order and scores: the directory this page lives in.
